messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-789123) — severity: high. Detected sustained GPU memory pressure on pool g-prod-rc1 in us-west-2. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, auto-shedder activity, elevated KV-cache evictions. Auto-remediation attempted: retry/backoff.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-789123 assigned to @mira_oncall (on-call). PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-789123

mira_oncall: acked — looking now. any quick wins before escalation? :thumbsup:

sam_infra: do we have a hotfix? if this is kv-cache thrash, draining the pool and shifting traffic to g-prod-rc2 might buy time.

leo_gpu: grabbing logs now — early signs show repeated alloc failures during long context requests. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T13:12:23Z] model=ggml-large req_id=abc123 ERROR CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 142MB for kv_cache (available 64MB)
[2026-03-15T13:12:24Z] eviction triggered: kv_cache entries=1.2M -> 1.0M
[2026-03-15T13:12:27Z] auto-shedder: shedding low-priority requests to meet latency SLOs
```

mira_oncall: ok runbook link?

sam_infra: runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/gpu-memory-pressure. I'm going to start a controlled drain of g-prod-rc1 and shift traffic to rc2/rc4. command:
```bash
redwoodctl pool drain --pool g-prod-rc1 --grace-period 30s --parallel 4
redwoodctl route shift --from g-prod-rc1 --to g-prod-rc2,g-prod-rc4 --pct 100
```

leo_gpu: noted. also adding a kernel-level guard to skip large-KV inferences for the next 20m: `RUNTIME_KV_SKIP=1` on the pool config.

mira_oncall: executing drain now. posting status updates.

sam_infra: started drain at 13:14:02Z. traffic shift in progress. watching autoscaler.

leo_gpu: metrics update ~2m after drain start — GPU mem free increased, alloc failure rate falling:
```
metric: cuda_alloc_failures/s 13:14 -> 13:18 : 62 -> 8
metric: kvcache_evictions/s     13:14 -> 13:18 : 420 -> 45
gpu_mem_used(percent)          13:14 -> 13:18 : 93% -> 68%
```

carla_sre: any customer-facing impact? CS asking for timeline + list of tenants impacted.

mira_oncall: early look: spike correlated with heavy long-context requests to model ggml-large in eu-west-1 routed through edge peering that backfills to us-west-2. Estimated affected requests: ~0.7% of all requests in the 10m window, with increased 503/504s on lower-priority plans. I'll pull exact query logs.

leo_gpu: found sample error traces from request ids: abc123, def456, ghi789 — all show identical OOM pattern and fallback responses from our API gateway.

mira_oncall: adding incident note to PagerDuty: customer impact = degraded for subset (low-priority) requests; mitigation = pool drained + traffic shifted; ETA to monitor = 20m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-789123 updated by @mira_oncall: "drain + traffic shift in progress; customer impact limited; monitoring"

sam_infra: scaled up dedicated capacity for g-prod-rc2 by +2 GPUs as a precaution: `redwoodctl capacity add --pool g-prod-rc2 --gpus 2`

leo_gpu: after capacity add, mem pressure leveled further. also disabled a recent kernel optimization flag that increased memory footprint on long sequences.

mira_oncall: good. can someone confirm no further OOMs in the last 2 minutes?

leo_gpu: checking — alloc failures: 2 in last 2m (non-fatal), compared to 62 at peak.

carla_sre: filing brief for CS: "small % of requests saw transient failures while on-call team drained an impacted GPU pool; no data exfiltration; mitigation applied." I'll send to ops-cc.

mira_oncall: adding follow-up action items to the incident:
- short term: run `redwoodctl pool health --pool g-prod-rc1` and keep drained until we validate lower mem footprint
- mid term: evaluate kv_cache eviction thresholds and auto-shedder heuristics for ggml-large
- long term: add per-tenant backpressure controls to avoid cross-tenant collateral on long context runs

sam_infra: running health check now:
```bash
redwoodctl pool health --pool g-prod-rc1 --verbose
# result: nodes=6, healthy=5, unstable=1 (high mem fragmentation), recommendations: recycle node n-3
```

leo_gpu: I kicked a recycle on n-3 and re-ran cuda driver init. logs show successful re-init and vmem stabilizing.

mira_oncall: thanks. I'm going to mark the incident as "mitigated" in PagerDuty and hand off to followup for postmortem. leaving this thread open for 30m for additional checks.

pagerduty-bot: PD-789123 status -> mitigated by @mira_oncall at 13:22:40Z.

carla_sre: noted. assigning postmortem to @sam_infra and @leo_gpu. please include root cause candidate list + timeline and the customer-impacted tenant list.

mira_oncall: handoff: I'm off in 40m — @sam_infra please own any further actions; I'll add notes to the PD ticket and to the incident board.

sam_infra: got it — taking ownership for followup. will schedule a postmortem and include suggested config changes.

leo_gpu: final check — no new OOMs in last 8m, KV evictions back to baseline. continuing to monitor.

mira_oncall: thanks everyone. summary to paste into PD: "GPU memory pressure on g-prod-rc1 triggered repeated CUDA OOMs during heavy long-context requests. Auto-shedder reduced load; we drained the pool and shifted traffic, recycled a fragmented node, scaled up capacity on g-prod-rc2, and disabled a memory-heavy kernel flag. Impact: transient failures for a small percentage of low-priority requests. Next: postmortem to tune kv_cache/auto-shedder and add per-tenant backpressure."

pagerduty-bot: PD-789123 will remain in mitigated state; please update the incident if status changes.

mira_oncall: closing note here — monitoring for 30m; will add SOC/CS communication row once we have exact tenant list. :white_check_mark:
